articles.title: Astronomers deliver the sharpest and deepest view yet of the low-frequency radio sky
articles.description: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies. The image reveals almost 63,000 radio sources, such as active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies, across a patch of sky about 25 times the area of the full moon. The results have been accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The paper is currently available on the arXiv preprint server.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Low Frequency Array (LOFAR) produces the sharpest and deepest view of the low-frequency radio sky to date, opening new windows for astronomical discovery.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has captured its first detailed images of the asteroids involved in NASA's historic 2022 DART impact experiment. This follow-up mission provides crucial data on how planetary defense technologies reshape celestial bodies.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone of traveling one light-day from Earth, nearly 50 years after launch. This remarkable probe continues functioning at the outer edges of our solar system, representing humanity's greatest journey of exploration.

articles.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
articles.description: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago. The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases of DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, suggesting the building blocks of life may be distributed throughout the cosmos. This breakthrough strengthens the panspermia hypothesis and expands our understanding of life's origins.

articles.title: NASA Voyager 1 Is About To Break A Huge Record — Here's When
articles.description: After nearly 50 years, Voyager 1 is about to reach a milestone no spacecraft has ever hit. Once that happens, a simple data exchange will take over two days.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone after nearly 50 years in space, about to achieve a record no spacecraft has ever reached. This extraordinary achievement celebrates humanity's most distant ambassador exploring the cosmos.

articles.title: A Mighty Wind Blew Away Gas and Made Early Galaxies Brighter
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. But these galaxies should have been far less common so soon after the Big Bang. Researchers may have figured this out: Powerful ultraviolet (Lyman-alpha) radiation produced by dense clusters of young stars acted like a leaf blower, driving light-blocking gas and dust out of the galaxy and thereby making the galaxies appear brighter.
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations reveal that powerful winds in the early universe stripped gas from galaxies, making them brighter and reshaping our understanding of galactic formation.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.description: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.
articles.summary: The interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS provides unprecedented evidence that water ice behaves consistently across different star systems, offering insights into universal chemistry.

articles.title: Exoplanets Can't Hide From The JWST's 'Digital Twin'
articles.description: Finding dim exoplanets hidden in the glare of their stars is an ongoing challenge in astronomy. Telescopes use coronagraphs to block out starlight, but even they have their limitations. Researchers have developed a new technique with the JWST that can find dim exoplanets more easily than ever.
articles.summary: New JWST technology using digital twin modeling enables astronomers to detect faint exoplanets hidden within the bright glare of their parent stars.

articles.title: China Unveils Their Plan for a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.description: Yesterday, on November 3rd, the deputy chief designer of China's crewed space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program (Wang Xiang) unveiled an official statement detailing its [plans for a crewed mission to the Moon](https://english.spacechina.com/n17212/c4744561/content.html).
articles.summary: China announces ambitious plans for crewed lunar missions, expanding humanity's presence on the Moon and advancing international space exploration efforts.

articles.title: A Virtual Lifeless Earth Will Help Scientists Find Life on Exoplanets
articles.description: Researchers have created a model lifeless Earth that couples the atmosphere with interior planetary processes. The model can reproduce Earth's modern habitable state without including life, showing that a planet that appears habitable isn't necessarily inhabited. The tool will be useful when and if the Habitable Worlds Observatory is launched, by helping identify false positives.
articles.summary: Scientists develop a virtual lifeless Earth model integrating atmospheric and planetary processes to better identify biosignatures when searching for life on exoplanets.

articles.title: Webb Space Telescope's little red dots could hold key to first black holes
articles.description: Johns Hopkins researchers searching the expanse of the universe for the existence of the first black holes are zeroing in on little red dots that may hold the key to the theoretical phenomenon.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Webb Space Telescope's detection of distant red objects offers crucial clues to understanding the formation of the universe's first black holes.

articles.title: European orbiter detects fresh hints of volcanic activity on Mars
articles.description: New evidence from gas seeping above volcanic rifts suggests Mars is not geologically dead deep inside, but merely sleeping. Fresh fissures along the Alba Mons region hint at active spots under the surface, where gases from inside the planet may be making their way up to the surface.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: European orbiter detects fresh volcanic activity signatures on Mars, revealing the planet remains geologically active beneath its surface. This discovery challenges the notion that Mars is completely dormant and opens new understanding of the Red Planet's interior.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative plan to extend the legendary Hubble Space Telescope's operational life and prevent its eventual re-entry. This daring rescue mission represents humanity's commitment to preserving one of science's greatest observatories.

articles.title: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
articles.description: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha. New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified evidence of a hidden companion star plowing through the atmosphere of the red supergiant Betelgeuse. This discovery explains mysterious disturbances observed in one of the sky's most prominent stars.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a historic distance record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, surpassing all previous rovers. This achievement demonstrates the rover's durability and the success of Mars exploration technology.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: IceCube detector has captured neutrinos with energy levels 10 billion times greater than solar neutrinos, revealing high-energy cosmic mysteries. These ghost particles provide new windows into extreme astrophysical phenomena across the universe.

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
articles.description: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a theoretical loophole in black hole physics that could potentially allow them to split apart under certain conditions. This finding challenges conventional understanding of black hole stability and opens new avenues for theoretical exploration.

articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.description: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.summary: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk have successfully installed the final Roll-Out Solar Array on the International Space Station. This milestone completes a major upgrade enhancing the ISS's power generation capacity for years of continued research.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space
articles.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is back in communication after the 49-year-old spacecraft briefly fell silent last month, during its interstellar-space mission.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, humanity's most distant spacecraft after 49 years, has successfully restored communications following a brief silence in interstellar space. This remarkable achievement demonstrates the resilience of pioneering deep-space exploration technology.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have achieved a breakthrough in a 42-year search by finding evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay event. This discovery opens new frontiers in understanding fundamental physics.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers have witnessed two different kinds of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented cosmic event. This rare observation provides new insights into the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship 42 Fired Its Engines for the Last Time. What Comes Next? [20:54]
articles.description: Ship 42 has fired its engines for the last time on the ground, and Elon Musk just made a promise about it that no Starship has ever kept. The FAA moved Flight 15. SpaceX hasn't said a date. We did, last episode, and the new one doesn't match ours. Musk also p…
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship 42 has completed its final ground engine test, marking a major milestone in the development of the next-generation fully reusable super heavy-lift launch system. Elon Musk has announced an exciting promise about the vehicle's future.

articles.title: 補給品從太空送達，美軍攜手 SpaceX 完成火箭貨運測試
articles.description: 美國空軍研究實驗室（AFRL）近日完成「火箭貨運」（Rocket Cargo）測試，將軍用補給品裝入 SpaceX Starfall 返回艙，經火箭發射升空後返回地球，為未來不依賴機場跑道的快速運補蒐集驗證資料。 With support from @SpaceX, the AFRL agile c...
articles.summary: The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory successfully completed the Rocket Cargo test with SpaceX, demonstrating rapid supply delivery capabilities using Starfall reentry vehicles. This breakthrough shows promise for fast logistics support independent of traditional airport infrastructure.

articles.title: Asteroids' Oddball Shapes Make Deflecting Them Challenging
articles.description: In a pinch, we could use a stand-off nuclear blast to redirect a dangerous asteroid on short notice. There's no atmospheric shock wave in space, but the x-ray pulse could still deflect the space rock. But asteroids aren't round and uniform, so their weird shapes make it difficult.
articles.summary: Scientists explore innovative methods for redirecting asteroids, including nuclear deflection techniques, to protect Earth from potentially hazardous space objects.

articles.title: Game Theory Helps SETI Search for Alien Civilizations
articles.description: SETI can be more effective the more the targets in the search are refined. SETI's newest survey effort uses game theory to inform its search. It's based on the idea that other ETIs would almost certainly use the transit method to detect habitable worlds like Earth.
articles.summary: SETI researchers apply game theory to refine target selection for searching alien civilizations, enhancing the efficiency of the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

articles.title: Giant Impacts Help Rocky Planets Retain Their Atmospheres
articles.description: For a long time, planetary scientists thought that giant impacts drove a young planet's atmosphere away into space with all the heat they generated. But it turns out the opposite could be true. The mass a young planet gains through a giant impact increases its gravitational hold on its atmosphere.
articles.summary: Planetary scientists discover that giant impacts may actually help young rocky planets retain their atmospheres, challenging previous assumptions about planetary formation.

articles.title: Connecting artificial intelligence with the tools of astrophysical research
articles.description: Investigating a scientific question is often a complex process. As an astrophysicist studying some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe, I know that finding answers requires much more than reading scientific papers or understanding existing theories. Astrophysical research involves collecting observations, analyzing data, building physical models and comparing their predictions with observations. These tasks require different scientific tools, databases and modeling software and can take considerable time even for experienced researchers.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence integration with astrophysical research tools accelerates the investigation of complex cosmic phenomena and energetic events.

articles.title: Hubble learns galactic history from stars
articles.description: This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image provides a lesson in galactic history. The sparkling collection of stars is named Messier 30 (M30) after the French astronomer Charles Messier, who cataloged M30 and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets in the early telescopes of Messier's time. M30 lies about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Hubble Space Telescope observations of stellar populations reveal galactic history and the evolutionary processes that shaped nearby galaxies.

articles.title: Earth's slowing spin may have shaped its primordial crust
articles.description: Around 4.5 billion years ago, a planet-sized object collided with the newly formed Earth, throwing out the debris that would later form the moon. The collision left Earth spinning extremely fast, with days lasting just two to five hours. Yet existing models of how Earth's first crust formed and evolved have largely overlooked how the planet's later slowdown might have affected it.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Research reveals that Earth's gradually slowing rotation 4.5 billion years ago influenced the formation and structure of the planet's primordial crust.

articles.title: Microbial growth in simulated Mars conditions could guide search for life
articles.description: A new experiment reveals that Earth's microbes can grow in harsh conditions similar to what may exist just below the surface of Mars, suggesting new directions in the search for potential cellular life on the red planet.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Laboratory experiments demonstrate that Earth microbes can survive in simulated Martian subsurface conditions, informing strategies for detecting life on Mars.
